talking_points.headline: Private banking desk-head hiring is turning into a zero-sum talent war across HSBC's home markets
talking_points.context_html: Tan Lay Hong, incoming HSBC Private Bank Singapore Desk Head, joins from UBS after 14 years there, one of at least three senior cross-bank private banking moves reported in Hong Kong and Singapore this week alone, alongside UOB's and RBC's hires from HSBC, Bank of China and Standard Chartered. With every major player drawing from the same shallow bench of desk heads simultaneously, retention needs a seat on the change-execution agenda alongside recruitment as HSBC scales its 200-hire Singapore build-out.
source_links: HSBC hires UBS veteran as Singapore desk head

talking_points.headline: HKMA puts a number on Hong Kong banks' quantum readiness — and it's a 2.3 out of 10
talking_points.context_html: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's first Quantum Preparedness Index score is a direct read on how exposed the sector — HSBC included — is to “harvest now, decrypt later” threats as quantum computing matures. It lands the same month HSBC is scaling agentic AI and stablecoin infrastructure across Hong Kong; operational resilience now has a public regulatory benchmark tracked to 2030, making this a strong candidate for the next change-execution risk review.
source_links: HKMA scores HK banks 2.3/10 on quantum readiness

talking_points.headline: Open-weight AI just got a 2.8-trillion-parameter upgrade — and the cost curve keeps bending
talking_points.context_html: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 — the largest open-weight model to date, priced at roughly a third of comparable closed models — arrives the same week Anthropic halved pricing with Opus 5. For a bank standing up its own AI Centre of Excellence in Singapore, the build-vs-buy and single-vendor-vs-multi-vendor maths for agentic AI is shifting weekly rather than quarterly, worth flagging directly into the CoE's model-sourcing strategy.
source_links: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3 open weights

HSBC News.title: HSBC Private Bank hires UBS veteran Tan Lay Hong as Singapore desk head
HSBC News.summary: HSBC Private Bank has hired 14-year UBS veteran Tan Lay Hong as Singapore Desk Head, reporting to market head Hammad Hashmi. The hire is one of at least three senior cross-bank private banking moves in Hong Kong and Singapore reported this week, as HSBC, UOB and RBC compete for the same shallow bench of desk heads.

Regulatory & Markets.title: HKMA scores Hong Kong banks 2.3 out of 10 on quantum readiness
Regulatory & Markets.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's first Quantum Preparedness Index scores the territory's banking sector 2.3 out of 10, with most lenders still at the awareness stage and lacking formal post-quantum migration plans. The HKMA is targeting a score of 10 by 2030 and will roll out toolkits, workshops and skills training to get the industry there.

Regulatory & Markets.title: HSBC's Kettner stays bullish on risk assets heading into results week
Regulatory & Markets.summary: HSBC chief multi-asset strategist Max Kettner reiterated his maximum-overweight call on global equities, citing strong Q2 earnings and a two-turn reset in forward valuations, while flagging stretched sentiment and US midterm uncertainty as reasons to trim exposure after this earnings season. The call lands days before both HSBC's own 4 August interim results and the Fed's 29 July rate decision.

AI & Technology.title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3, the largest open-weight model to date
AI & Technology.summary: Moonshot AI released open weights for Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter model under a permissive Modified MIT licence, matching Claude-class coding performance at roughly a third of the cost while running about four times slower. The release lands the same week Anthropic halved its own pricing with Opus 5, compressing the cost curve for frontier-adjacent AI further.
